title: the Poincare conjecture, topological form
source_location: MT Cor 0.2(a), Introduction, p. x, with footnote 1, p. ix (topological 3-manifolds are smoothable)
hol_theorems: POINCARE_TOP (|- POINCARE_STATEMENT (:A)); POINCARE_FROM_SMOOTH_AND_MOISE; POINCARE_SMOOTH; MOI_SST_HEADLINE; statement POINCARE_STATEMENT
notes: Every compact, Hausdorff, nonempty, simply connected topological space that is locally Euclidean of dimension 3 is homeomorphic to the unit sphere of R^4. Stated for a type variable A, so it holds for spaces on every carrier type, with the small definitions of src/poincare_statement.ml over the HOL Light topology library (simply_connected_space mirrors the library's simply_connected for sets). Proof: Moise's theorem gives a smooth atlas for the given topology (MOI_SST_HEADLINE) and the smooth form then gives a homeomorphism onto S^3 (POINCARE_FROM_SMOOTH_AND_MOISE). MT state the smooth form and cite the smoothing of topological 3-manifolds (footnote 1). The Qin theorem is the same statement in Mathlib's notions; FrenzyMath obtain a homeomorphic smooth model instead of a smooth atlas on the given space.

title: the Poincare conjecture, smooth form: a closed simply connected smooth 3-manifold is diffeomorphic to S^3
hol_theorems: POINCARE_SMOOTH (|- POINCARE_SMOOTH_STATEMENT (:A)); RFS_POINCARE_SMOOTH; METRIC_EXISTENCE; RFS_EXTINCTION; EVENT_TOPOLOGY; RFS_CUTCAP_SC; RFS_LISTED_SC_S3; RFS_SPHERE_SYSTEM; SMT_POINCARE_CONVERSION; statement POINCARE_SMOOTH_STATEMENT
notes: Every compact, Hausdorff, nonempty, simply connected space with a smooth 3-dimensional atlas (second countability is not assumed) admits a smooth immersion into R^4 that is a homeomorphism onto the unit sphere, that is, it is diffeomorphic to the standard S^3. Proof (RFS_POINCARE_SMOOTH): a Riemannian metric from a Whitney embedding (METRIC_EXISTENCE); a controlled Ricci flow with surgery that becomes extinct (RFS_EXTINCTION: Thm 15.9, Cor 15.10 and Thm 18.1 in the simply connected case); the topology of each surgery event (Prop 15.3: EVENT_TOPOLOGY, RFS_CUTCAP_SC, RFS_LISTED_SC_S3); backward induction from the empty last stage (Cor 15.4(2): RFS_SPHERE_SYSTEM); and the conversion of a diffeomorphism with the standard S^3 into the immersion form (SMT_POINCARE_CONVERSION).

title: the topological Poincare conjecture for subsets of R^N
source_location: MT Cor 0.2(a), p. x (a corollary stated with library notions only)
hol_theorems: POINCARE_EMBEDDED (|- POINCARE_EMBEDDED_STATEMENT (:N)); POINCARE_STATEMENT_IMP_EMBEDDED; statement POINCARE_EMBEDDED_STATEMENT
notes: Every compact, nonempty, simply connected subset M of R^N (the library's simply_connected) in which every point has a relatively open neighbourhood homeomorphic to R^3 is homeomorphic to the unit sphere of R^4. It uses only notions of the HOL Light library and follows from POINCARE_TOP at the type real^N (POINCARE_STATEMENT_IMP_EMBEDDED).

title: Moise's theorem: compact topological 3-manifolds have smooth atlases
source_location: Moise Thm 35.3, Sec 35, p. 252, and Thm 36.1, Sec 36, p. 253; MT p. ix, footnote 1
hol_theorems: MOI_SST_HEADLINE (|- !u. MOISE_SMOOTHING_STATEMENT u); MOI_MOISE_SMOOTHING_FROM_CORES; MOI_CORE_STATUS; MOI_SST_SMOOTH; statement MOISE_SMOOTHING_STATEMENT
notes: Every compact Hausdorff space that is locally Euclidean of dimension 3 has a smooth atlas whose charts are homeomorphisms for the given topology. It follows from two cores (MOI_MOISE_SMOOTHING_FROM_CORES): Moise 35.2 for locally finite combinatorial 3-manifolds in R^7 with target R^3 (MOI_CORE_STATUS), which gives a PL atlas by chart gluing (Thms 35.3 and 36.1, compact case), and the smoothing of finite combinatorial 3-manifolds (MOI_SST_SMOOTH, row SMOOTHING-PL). The Qin theorem is the same statement; FrenzyMath prove that every compact connected topological 3-manifold has a homeomorphic smooth model, following Hamilton 1976 and Cairns 1940.

title: a closed simply connected 3-manifold of constant curvature 1 is the round S^3 (the case of the uniformization theorem used)
hol_theorems: KILLING_HOPF_S3_ISOMETRY (|- KILLING_HOPF_S3_STATEMENT (:A)); KILLING_HOPF_S3; KILLING_HOPF_COMPONENT; statement KILLING_HOPF_S3_STATEMENT
notes: Only the case the proof needs: n = 3, lambda = 1, M compact, nonempty and simply connected, with an isometry onto the unit sphere of R^4 (Killing-Hopf). KILLING_HOPF_S3 is the diffeomorphism form and KILLING_HOPF_COMPONENT the form for one connected component, used for the round components that are discarded at surgery times. Proof: two Cartan maps from S^3 minus a point agree near a point, glue to a local isometry S^3 --> M, which is a local homeomorphism onto a simply connected manifold and hence bijective. Cases (1) and (3) (flat and hyperbolic) are not formalized.

title: minimizing geodesics: proper initial arcs are unique minimizers and have no conjugate points
hol_theorems: CMP_MINIMIZING_GEODESIC (|- !u n. CMP_MINIMIZING_GEODESIC_STATEMENT u n); statement CMP_MINIMIZING_GEODESIC_STATEMENT
notes: In every dimension N. Along a minimizing geodesic the restrictions to [0,t], t < 1, are the unique minimizers between their endpoints and d exp_x is nonsingular at t v for t < 1 (no conjugate points). The proof uses the second variation of energy for piecewise smooth variations (the index form, src/pc_cmp_index.ml) and Jacobi's theorem.

title: conjugate radius under an upper curvature bound
hol_theorems: CMP_CONJUGATE_RADIUS (|- !u n. CMP_CONJUGATE_RADIUS_STATEMENT u n); statement CMP_CONJUGATE_RADIUS_STATEMENT
notes: The printed lemma has no completeness or compact-closure hypothesis and is false without one (the flat open unit ball with K = 1: exp_p is not defined on the tangent ball of radius pi); MT restate it with compact closure on p. 50, the form used for Thm 3.29. HOL assumes that the tangent ball of radius pi/sqrt K lies in the domain of exp_x and only sec <= K there (weaker than abs(Rm) <= K), and concludes that d exp_x is injective on that ball and exp_x is a local diffeomorphism there.

title: Ricci curvature comparison for the volume density and the Laplacian of distance functions
hol_theorems: CMP_LAPLACIAN_BARRIER (|- !u n. CMP_LAPLACIAN_BARRIER_STATEMENT u n); CMP_LAPLACIAN_BARRIER_SQ; CMP_RELVOL; statement CMP_LAPLACIAN_BARRIER_STATEMENT
notes: The density comparison det g(r,theta) <= sn^(n-1) (Bishop) is proved inside the relative volume comparison (CMP_RELVOL, Thm 1.34): the ratio of the exp-pullback density to the model density is at most 1 and non-increasing along rays. The Laplacian part is proved in Calabi's barrier form: under Ric >= -(n-1)K on a complete manifold, d_p has at every x <> p a smooth upper barrier with gradient of norm 1 and Laplacian at most (n-1)(1/d + sqrt K) + e for every e > 0, and d_p^2 has one at every point (CMP_LAPLACIAN_BARRIER_SQ).

title: relative volume comparison (Bishop-Gromov)
hol_theorems: CMP_RELVOL (|- !u n. CMP_RELVOL_STATEMENT u n); CMP_T1_BISHOP_GROMOV; CMP_T3_BISHOP_GROMOV_P2B; statement CMP_RELVOL_STATEMENT
notes: In every dimension N, in the local form printed: B(x,R) with compact closure and Ric >= -(n-1)K on it give v2 V_{-K}(r1) <= v1 V_{-K}(r2) for 0 < r1 <= r2 <= R (the ratio Vol B(x,r)/V_{-K}(r) is non-increasing) and the absolute bound Vol B(x,r) <= V_{-K}(r). Proof without polar coordinates: the volume of a ball is the integral of the exp-pullback density over the injective part of the segment domain, compared with the model by a radial change of variables. CMP_T1_BISHOP_GROMOV and CMP_T3_BISHOP_GROMOV_P2B are the K = 0 forms used in Chapters 9 and 12.

title: volume lower bound from the injectivity radius
hol_theorems: CMP_GUNTHER (|- !u n. CMP_GUNTHER_STATEMENT u n); statement CMP_GUNTHER_STATEMENT
notes: HOL proves the Gunther-Bishop inequality that underlies the proposition: if sec <= K on an injectivity ball B(x,r) with r sqrt K <= pi, then Vol B(x,r) >= V_K(r), the volume of the ball of radius r in the model space of curvature K. With K = r^-2 this gives the printed bound with an explicit delta; no completeness is needed.

title: injectivity radius lower bound from a volume lower bound (Cheeger-Gromov-Taylor)
hol_theorems: CMP_T2_CGT (|- !u. CMP_T2_CGT_STATEMENT u); statement CMP_T2_CGT_STATEMENT
notes: Local form in dimension 3: for K, r, v0 > 0 there is i0 in (0,r) such that whenever B(x,r) has compact closure, abs(Rm) <= K on it and Vol B(x,r) >= v0, the injectivity radius at x is at least i0. Completeness is replaced by compact closure of the ball, and the constant depends on (K, r, v0); the scale-invariant printed form follows by rescaling. Used for the compactness theorems of Chapter 5.

title: Toponogov comparison in non-negative curvature
hol_theorems: CMP_R1_TOPONOGOV (|- !w. CMP_R1_TOPONOGOV_STATEMENT w); CMP_R8_LOCAL_TOPONOGOV; statements CMP_R1_TOPONOGOV_STATEMENT, CMP_R8_LOCAL_TOPONOGOV_STATEMENT
notes: Angle form under sec >= 0 on a complete manifold: for two minimizing unit-speed geodesics from p the cosine of the comparison angle (s1^2 + s2^2 - d^2)/(2 s1 s2) is non-decreasing in each length; the hinge form is its limit. CMP_R8_LOCAL_TOPONOGOV is a local form needing only shortest curves inside a region, used on incomplete limits in Chapter 10. The proof uses the concavity of t --> d(q, sigma(t))^2 - t^2, obtained from Calabi barriers.

title: soul theorem, positively curved case
hol_theorems: CMP_R5_SOUL (|- !w. CMP_R5_SOUL_STATEMENT w); CMP_R6_REGULAR_FIELD; statements CMP_R5_SOUL_STATEMENT, CMP_R6_REGULAR_FIELD_STATEMENT
notes: Only the case used (sec > 0, the soul is a point): a complete connected noncompact 3-manifold with sec > 0 has a point p such that every other point is regular for d_p (Gromoll-Meyer). The supremum of the Busemann functions of the rays from a base point is convex and proper, its minimum is unique, and at every other point some ray has an asymptote obtuse to all minimizing directions to p. CMP_R6_REGULAR_FIELD gives near every compact set of regular points a smooth unit vector field making a uniformly obtuse angle with all minimizing directions to p (the isotopy lemma). The general soul theorem (normal bundle of a soul) is not formalized; the Qin theorem is the general one.

title: splitting theorem
hol_theorems: CMP_R3_SPLIT (|- !w. CMP_R3_SPLIT_STATEMENT w); statement CMP_R3_SPLIT_STATEMENT
notes: Form used on the route: a complete connected manifold with sec >= 0 containing a line is locally split, with a parallel unit vector field tangent to the line (the Busemann functions of the two halves are convex, their sum vanishes, so they are affine along geodesics). MT state it for Ric >= 0 and two ends (giving N x R with N compact); on the route the curvature is sec >= 0 and two ends give a line, and the splitting is used through the parallel field. No elliptic regularity is needed.

title: positively curved complete 3-manifolds have no epsilon-necks of arbitrarily small scale
hol_theorems: P2AS_PROP_2_19_SEP (|- !u. P2_PROP_2_19_SEP_STATEMENT u); statement P2_PROP_2_19_SEP_STATEMENT
notes: The printed statement needs connectedness: a disjoint union of shrinking positively curved ellipsoids is complete and positively curved and has epsilon-necks at arbitrarily small scales. HOL proves, for connected complete 3-manifolds, the form used on blow-up limits (pp. 278, 407): sec >= 0 instead of sec > 0, together with the hypothesis that the central sphere of every neck chart separates; then R is bounded at all centres of epsilon-necks. The proof uses Toponogov comparison instead of Hamilton's strong maximum principle, which the printed application to limits with only Rm >= 0 would need.

title: short-time existence and uniqueness of Ricci flow on compact manifolds
hol_theorems: PDEF_STE (|- !u n. PDE_STE_STATEMENT u n); PDE_UNIQUENESS (|- !u n. PDE_UNIQUENESS_STATEMENT u n); PDEF_MAXIMAL_FLOW; PDEF_STE_UNIFORM; statements PDE_STE_STATEMENT, PDE_UNIQUENESS_STATEMENT, PDE_MAXIMAL_FLOW_STATEMENT
notes: In every dimension N, for compact Hausdorff smooth manifolds and any initial time a: a flow from g0 exists on some [a,b) and is smooth up to time a, and two flows from the same metric agree on the common interval. MT sketch existence and only cite uniqueness. Existence goes through the Ricci-DeTurck flow (linear parabolic systems on a torus model solved by the continuity method from the heat equation, then an iteration for the Ricci-DeTurck system, in the src/pc_pde_ files), and the gauge is removed with the flow of the DeTurck vector field, with the sign of Chow-Lu-Ni (the sketch in MT has the opposite sign); uniqueness is Kotschwar's energy method (e = abs(h)^2 + abs(A)^2 + abs(S)^2 for the differences of metrics, connections and curvatures, divergence theorem and Gronwall), as in both Lean proofs.

title: gluing Ricci flows in time
hol_theorems: PDE_GLUE (|- !u n. PDE_GLUE_STATEMENT u n); statement PDE_GLUE_STATEMENT
notes: On any manifold and in every dimension: a flow on (a,b) whose chart matrices converge with all spatial derivatives, locally uniformly, to those of g(b) as t --> b-, followed by a flow from g(b) on [b,c), is a smooth flow on (a,c). The time derivatives at t = b are obtained by expressing them through spatial derivatives with the flow equation.

title: distances are non-increasing under non-negative Ricci curvature
hol_theorems: P2AR_LEMMA_3_14 (|- !u. P2_LEMMA_3_14_STATEMENT u); statement P2_LEMMA_3_14_STATEMENT
notes: Dimension 3, Ricci flow on (a,b) with Ric >= 0: d_{g(t2)}(x,y) <= d_{g(t1)}(x,y) for t1 <= t2. The connectedness hypothesis of the printed lemma is not needed. Used on the standard solution in Lemma 17.7.

title: time derivative of distance under an upper Ricci bound
source_location: MT Prop 3.21 and Claim 3.24, Sec 3.6, pp. 45-46
hol_theorems: RFA_P2B_REQ_RFA_DIST_LOCAL (|- !u n. P2B_REQ_RFA_DIST_LOCAL_STATEMENT u n); CMP_RICCI_INTEGRAL (|- !u n. CMP_RICCI_INTEGRAL_STATEMENT u n); statements P2B_REQ_RFA_DIST_LOCAL_STATEMENT, CMP_RICCI_INTEGRAL_STATEMENT
notes: Local form with a backward difference quotient, in every dimension n: if the slice at t is complete, d_t(x0,x1) >= 2 r0 and Ric <= (n-1)K on the two balls of radius r0, then for every e > 0, d_{t-s}(x0,x1) <= d_t(x0,x1) + s(2(n-1)(K r0 + 1/r0) + e) for all small s > 0. The constant K r0 replaces the printed (2/3) K r0 (a weaker bound that suffices for the uses). Claim 3.24 (the integral of Ric along a minimizing geodesic) is CMP_RICCI_INTEGRAL, proved by the second variation with the trapezoid test function; the case d < 2 r0 is handled with the whole geodesic in the two end balls.

title: Shi's local derivative estimates
hol_theorems: RFA_P2_THM_3_28 (|- !u. P2_THM_3_28_STATEMENT u); statement P2_THM_3_28_STATEMENT
notes: Dimension 3, in the form used on the route: for l, K, r, tau > 0 there is C_l such that for every flow on (a,b], smooth up to b, on a possibly incomplete manifold, with b - a >= tau, a ball B(x,b,r) with compact closure and abs(Rm) <= K on it over (a,b], one has abs(nabla^l Rm) <= C_l on B(x,b,r/2) at time b. MT state the bound C_k/t^(k/2) for all t in (0,T] on the half ball at time 0 under T <= alpha/K; the final-time form with a constant depending on the elapsed time tau is what the applications (necks, Lemma 11.21, Claim 16.6) use. The proof goes order by order on shrinking parabolic regions, in normal coordinates at each centre.

title: Shi's estimates with initial derivative bounds
hol_theorems: RFA_P2_THM_3_29 (|- !u. P2_THM_3_29_STATEMENT u); statement P2_THM_3_29_STATEMENT
notes: Dimension 3: if abs(Rm) <= K on B(x,a,r) for t in [a,b), b - a <= tau, the ball has compact closure and abs(nabla^j Rm) <= K at time a on the ball for j <= l, then abs(nabla^j Rm) <= C_l on B(x,a,r/2) for all j <= l and t in [a,b), with no blow-up at t = a. This is the case k <= l of the printed theorem, with the curvature bound required only on the ball (MT ask for it on all of U); it is the case used at the surgery caps (Lemma 16.8, Cor 16.9).

title: the minimum of the scalar curvature is non-decreasing on closed manifolds
hol_theorems: RFA_P2C_REQ_SCALAR_MIN (|- !u. P2C_REQ_SCALAR_MIN_STATEMENT u); RFA_P2A_REQ_RLOWER (|- !u. P2A_REQ_RLOWER_STATEMENT u); statements P2C_REQ_SCALAR_MIN_STATEMENT, P2A_REQ_RLOWER_STATEMENT
notes: Dimension 3, closed manifolds: the first bullet (for t1 <= t2 every value R(x,t2) is at least R(y,t1) for some y, i.e. R_min is non-decreasing) and the lower bound R >= min(0, R_min(a)). Both come from the evolution inequality dR/dt >= Lap R + (2/n) R^2 and the minimum principle (src/pc_rfa_scalar.ml). The explicit lower barriers of the other bullets enter the route through (4.6) of Thm 4.32 instead.

title: curvature bound, existence time and non-collapsing from normalized initial conditions
source_location: MT Def 4.10 and Prop 4.11, Sec 4.3, p. 67
hol_theorems: PV411_PROP_4_11_VOLUME (|- !u. P2_PROP_4_11_VOLUME_STATEMENT u); PDEF_CURVATURE_TIME (|- !u n. PDE_CURVATURE_TIME_STATEMENT u n); statements P2_PROP_4_11_VOLUME_STATEMENT, PDE_CURVATURE_TIME_STATEMENT, rfs_normalized
notes: Split into a curvature part and a volume part. Curvature part: the flow from a metric with abs(Rm) <= 1 exists and has abs(Rm) <= C on [0,c] for dimensional constants c, C; the printed constants 2^-4 and 2 depend on a norm abs(Rm) that MT never define, so they are existential. Volume part: on a closed 3-manifold, from a normalized metric (rfs_normalized: abs(Rm) <= 1 and Vol B(x,r) >= (omega_3/2) r^3 for all r <= 1, as in Def 4.10) with abs(Rm) <= K on [0,tau], the flow is kappa0-noncollapsed on scales <= 1 with kappa0 depending on (K, tau).

title: a flow on a compact manifold extends unless the curvature is unbounded
hol_theorems: PDEF_EXTENSION (|- !u n. PDE_EXTENSION_STATEMENT u n); PDEF_MAXIMAL_FLOW; statements PDE_EXTENSION_STATEMENT, PDE_MAXIMAL_FLOW_STATEMENT
notes: In every dimension N on compact Hausdorff manifolds: a flow on [a,b) with abs(Rm) bounded extends past b. PDEF_MAXIMAL_FLOW combines it with existence and uniqueness: the flow from g0 exists for all time or on a maximal [a,b) with unbounded curvature, the form used by the slabs of a surgery history. MT cite this; the proof uses Hamilton's global derivative estimates (chart C^m bounds uniform in time) and short-time existence with a uniform existence time.

title: non-negative curvature is preserved on closed 3-manifolds
hol_theorems: RFA_P2C_REQ_SEC_PRESERVED (|- !u. P2C_REQ_SEC_PRESERVED_STATEMENT u); statement P2C_REQ_SEC_PRESERVED_STATEMENT
notes: Rm >= 0 is stated as sec >= 0, which is equivalent in dimension 3 (every 2-vector in dimension 3 is decomposable). Connectedness is not needed. Used for the compact approximations of the standard solution.

title: strong maximum principle for the heat equation
hol_theorems: RFA_STRONG_MAXP_SCALAR (|- !u n. RFA_STRONG_MAXP_SCALAR_STATEMENT u n); statement RFA_STRONG_MAXP_SCALAR_STATEMENT
notes: Proved in the form needed for scalar quantities along a Ricci flow on a connected manifold, without completeness (Chow-Lu-Ni Thm 6.54): the set of points where a non-negative supersolution is positive at all later times is open and closed. It feeds the strong maximum principle for R in Thm 4.18 and for the curvature operator in Cor 4.20.

title: strong maximum principle: R = 0 at one point forces flatness; a zero Ricci eigenvalue forces a local splitting
source_location: MT Thm 4.18 and Cor 4.19, Sec 4.4, p. 71
hol_theorems: RFA_P2B_REQ_SMP_SPLIT_PT (|- !w. P2B_REQ_RFA_SMP_SPLIT_PT_STATEMENT w); statement P2B_REQ_RFA_SMP_SPLIT_PT_STATEMENT
notes: Dimension 3, sec >= 0, connected and possibly incomplete. The dichotomy flat / locally split is stated at each time separately (an incomplete flow can be flat up to some time and split after it), and a zero of R at (p,t1) makes the flow flat on (a,t1]. A local splitting is a parallel unit vector field near every point, with smooth chart representatives. Used for the asymptotic soliton, Prop 9.83, Thm 9.64 and Lemma 9.65.

title: strong maximum principle for the curvature operator
hol_theorems: RFA_P2C_REQ_SMP_POS (|- !u. P2C_REQ_SMP_POS_STATEMENT u); statement P2C_REQ_SMP_POS_STATEMENT
notes: The local form used for the standard solution (Lemma 12.6, Thm 12.5(3)): on a connected 3-manifold, a flow with sec >= 0 on [a,b) and sec > 0 at one point at time a has sec > 0 everywhere at all times t > a. No completeness or compactness is assumed; the splitting of a cover in the zero-eigenvalue case is not needed.

title: a non-negatively curved flow that is a cone at the final time is flat
hol_theorems: RFA_P2B_REQ_CONE (|- !w. P2B_REQ_RFA_CONE_STATEMENT w); statement P2B_REQ_RFA_CONE_STATEMENT
notes: Dimension 3, sec >= 0 on (a,0], U connected and possibly incomplete. The cone hypothesis is stated analytically: a positive smooth function rho with Hess(rho^2/2) = g at the final time (the radial function of a Riemannian cone, which is what an open subset of a cone provides); the conclusion is that the flow is flat (all sectional curvatures vanish) on (a,0]. Used in the proof of Thm 10.2 (cone limits near the end).

title: positive curvature on closed 3-manifolds is preserved and pinches toward round
hol_theorems: RFA_P2_THM_4_23 (|- !u. P2_THM_4_23_STATEMENT u); RFA_P2B_REQ_PINCH_ROUND3 (|- !w. P2B_REQ_PINCH_ROUND3_STATEMENT w); statements P2_THM_4_23_STATEMENT, P2B_REQ_PINCH_ROUND3_STATEMENT
notes: The first sentence is false as printed: on round S^2 x flat S^1 with g(t) = (1-2t) g_S2 + d theta^2 one has Ric >= 0, neither Ric > 0 nor Ric = 0 (Hamilton's statement has a third, locally split case). HOL proves the two facts the route uses. P2_THM_4_23_STATEMENT: positive sectional curvature on a connected component of a closed 3-manifold is preserved (Cor 4.14 and the strong maximum principle; this is the use on p. 393). P2B_REQ_PINCH_ROUND3_STATEMENT: Hamilton's pinching for ancient compact flows, sec > 0 with sup sec <= (1+e) inf sec at very negative times forces constant curvature (estimate of the traceless Ricci tensor, then Schur), used for Cor 9.44.

title: Hamilton-Ivey pinching is preserved
hol_theorems: RFA_P2_THM_4_32 (|- !u. P2_THM_4_32_STATEMENT u); RFA_HI_PINCH_PRESERVED; statement P2_THM_4_32_STATEMENT; definition rfs_pinched_at
notes: Compact Hausdorff smooth 3-manifold, Ricci flow on [a,b) with a >= 0. rfs_pinched_at (src/pc_rfs_geom.ml) is (4.6)-(4.7) at time t with X = max(0,-nu), nu the least sectional curvature: the eigenvalues of Rm are read in the sectional normalization, the one in which the printed inequalities hold (with eigenvalues twice the sectional curvatures, (4.7) would be stronger than Hamilton's estimate). Proof by the weak maximum principle for the pinching function (1+t)R/2 - h(max(1,(1+t)X)), h(y) = y(log y - 3), with a Rayleigh-quotient barrier for the least eigenvalue. The Qin theorem is Hamilton's form, from a lower bound K on the curvature operator at t0.

title: Hamilton's trace Harnack inequality; dR/dt >= 0 on ancient solutions
source_location: MT Thm 4.37 and Cor 4.39, Sec 4.5, p. 81
hol_theorems: RFA_P2B_REQ_RFA_HARNACK (|- !w. P2B_REQ_RFA_HARNACK_STATEMENT w); P2AE_REQ_HARNACK (|- !u. P2C_REQ_HARNACK_STATEMENT u); P2B_KSOL_DRDT_FROM_HARNACK; RFA_HARNACK_MATRIX; statements P2B_REQ_RFA_HARNACK_STATEMENT, P2C_REQ_HARNACK_STATEMENT, P2B_KSOL_DRDT_STATEMENT
notes: Dimension 3, with sec >= 0 for Rm >= 0 (equivalent in dimension 3): for a complete flow on (a,b] with bounded curvature, dR/dt + R/(t-a) + 2 <X, grad R> + 2 Ric(X,X) >= 0 for every vector X, and in particular dR/dt + R/(t-a) >= 0. It is obtained from Hamilton's matrix Harnack inequality (RFA_HARNACK_MATRIX) by tracing, starting at a + eps and letting eps --> 0. Cor 4.39 (dR/dt >= 0 for ancient solutions) follows by letting a --> -infinity (P2B_KSOL_DRDT_FROM_HARNACK).

title: Cheeger-Gromov compactness for based Riemannian manifolds
source_location: MT Thm 5.6, Lemma 5.7, Thm 5.9 and Cor 5.10, Sec 5.1, pp. 85-88
hol_theorems: P2CK_CG_COMPACT (|- !u. P2C_CG_COMPACT_STATEMENT u (:real^3)); P2C_GAUGE (|- !u. P2C_GAUGE_STATEMENT u); statements P2C_CG_COMPACT_STATEMENT, P2C_GAUGE_STATEMENT
notes: Proved for the sequences that occur: time slices of surgery histories rescaled by Q_n, with balls of every radius having compact closure, all derivatives of Rm bounded on them and a volume lower bound at the base point; a subsequence converges smoothly on compact sets to a complete based 3-manifold carried by the type real^3. The injectivity radius bound comes from Thm 1.36 (CMP_T2_CGT) and the packing from Thm 1.34; the embeddings are obtained by patching inverse normal charts of the sequence over the charts of the glued limit with smooth cutoffs, and re-indexed along a diagonal subsequence. Lemma 5.7 (the gauge fixing of a limit) is P2C_GAUGE.

title: geometric limits of rescaled time slices of generalized flows

notes: For compact Hausdorff spaces locally Euclidean of dimension 3: there is a PL atlas (charts into R^3 with PL transition maps), and in simplicial form a combinatorial triangulation by a finite complex in R^7. The non-compact case is not needed.

notes: The polyhedron of a finite combinatorial 3-manifold has a smooth atlas (compatible with its topology; no compatibility with the PL structure is asked or needed), hence every compact Hausdorff space with a 3-dimensional PL atlas is smoothable. Route by metric smoothing: each tetrahedron gets the flat metric of a regular tetrahedron, the angles around each edge are rescaled, and near each vertex the structure is a cone over a smoothing of the vertex link, a polyhedral 2-sphere (the 2-dimensional chain of src/pc_moi_pd2_*.ml: no folds along creases, conical blow-ups of degree +1 or -1, a local homeomorphism onto S^2 is a homeomorphism). The Qin proof smooths handle by handle; FrenzyMath use Hamilton 1976 and Cairns 1940 instead of Moise and a separate smoothing.
